blind_reader_rulings.item: R4 item 6 / question (a) — preposition: reader prefers «по традициям» or «в традиции»
blind_reader_rulings.reason: «возвести/построить в традициях + gen.» is the established Russian collocation for architectural style (e.g. «в традициях русского зодчества»), and it is correct Russian. «по традициям» sounds more procedural (following rules or customs) and is not more accurate. The singular «в традиции» is acceptable but no better, and the source plural «طريقة/manner» does not decide between them. In rounds 2 and 3 the same reader frame «в традициях местного зодчества» passed without remark on the preposition, so the stumble comes from the noun that follows (see b), not from «в». BRIEF locks the lead-in except for a grammatical defect, and none exists.

blind_reader_rulings.item: R4 items 6–7 / question (b) — «зодчества Залива» and «регион Залива» read as un-Russian; reader expects «Персидского залива»
blind_reader_rulings.ruling: REJECTED — keep both; nativeness cost scored (-1 extra).
blind_reader_rulings.reason: Termbase entry «the Gulf» (sourced project decision 2026-09-05, matching zh 海湾 and de Golfregion) bars «Персидский залив». The rubric excludes overruling a sourced entry on fluency alone. In-termbase alternatives were weighed. «зодчества региона Залива» adds weight, and with the gloss gives «регион» twice. «зодчества стран Залива» projects modern states onto a historical building tradition; round 3 rejected it for the same reason in the gloss. «традиционным для Залива способом» (stage-4 fallback) still uses bare «Залива» and swaps a collocation for a heavier adverbial. None is clearly better, and each would reopen the locked lead-in on taste. Keeping «Залива» in both places is also deliberate: one Gulf frame links the method to the import, and that link is the whole point of round 4.

blind_reader_rulings.item: R4 item 7 / question (c) — «когда-то привозили» prompts 'and not now?'
blind_reader_rulings.ruling: REJECTED — faithful; this inference belongs to the source.
blind_reader_rulings.reason: «когда-то» renders «كان» / «once». The source itself marks the import as historical, so 'and not now?' is exactly what the source implies. Dropping «когда-то» would erase a distinction the Arabic makes (the import was a past practice, not a standing property of the wood). Replacements such as «издавна» (suggests the practice continues) or «в прошлом» (same meaning, no gain) either add meaning or change nothing. Saying whether the import still happens would add a fact the fence excludes.

blind_reader_rulings.item: R4 item 7 / question (d) — 'Gulf tradition + imported timber: where is the line between local and imported?'
blind_reader_rulings.ruling: REJECTED as a translation defect. It is a stable reader inference from a true, sourced pairing that the source itself states. Logged for Eyad as a source-level observation.
blind_reader_rulings.reason: Both sources now say verbatim: built in the traditional Gulf manner, with timber once imported to the Gulf. The Russian reproduces that pairing exactly and adds nothing. Across four rounds the reader's complaint changed in kind and then levelled off. R1: a false claim (all materials local → contradiction); a real defect, fixed. R2: an open question (local or imported?), answered by the source gloss. R3: tension between 'local tradition' and 'imported'. R4: the same tension, even though the frame is now explicitly Gulf-wide and the import is explicitly 'to the Gulf', so logically there is no opposition left. Every reader paired 'tradition' with 'imported' as opposites whatever the intro said, in three languages. That marks the pairing as a property of the information, not of any wording. The round-3 ru and zh judges ruled the same. Removing the tension would require either dropping the gloss (reverses an owner decision and erases source content) or adding that imported timber was normal in Gulf building, or naming its origin (facts the BRIEF fences out). The reader's own suggestion «которое завозили в эти края морем» adds 'by sea' and drops 'to the Gulf'; he conditions it on the source supporting it, and the source does not.

blind_reader_rulings.reason: Neither source names the species or the origin (BRIEF: the origin is disputed and must not be stated). «дерева» already marks it as wood.
